name: Fluency of Ideas
definition: The ability to come up with a number of ideas about a topic (the number of ideas is important, not their quality, correctness, or creativity).

benchmark.name: NoveltyBench
benchmark.metric: distinct_10: mean number of distinct responses out of 10 generations per prompt (scale 0-10)
benchmark.human_reference: General adult workforce: typical workers asked to generate several different responses or ideas on an everyday open-ended prompt, such as picking random items, naming examples, writing short creative pieces, or giving subjective opinions.

benchmark.name: NoveltyBench
benchmark.metric: NoveltyBench Distinct (mean number of distinct equivalence classes out of k=10 samples), NB-Curated split
benchmark.human_reference: General adult workforce performing ideation or brainstorming tasks. The comparison is to a typical adult asked to give 10 different responses to an open-ended prompt such as a joke, a story premise, a name, or a random pick.
